Junayed Ahmed Chowdhury, Advocate ----- For the Petitioners. 
Md Bahar Uddin-al-Razi, Advocate ----- For the Respondent No.1.
parties:
Begum Sitara Chowdhury and others ------ Petitioners 
Vs
Rajdhani Unnaiyan Kartipakka (RAJUK) and others ------ Respondents
full_judgment: 26. The Petitioners relying heavily on the ratio in the DIF Housing Case; have convinced this Court that in the instant case the 1953 Act lays down clear objectives ensuring the orderly development of Dhaka City through the agency of RAJUK. However, there is no authority reposed in RAJUK, as sought to be arrogated both at the First and Second Impugned Meetings, to blatantly misuse its power under the 1953 Act and unlawfully demand large sums of money disguised as conversion charge and converting that piece of legislation to an income earning device. It is this Court's view that such purported levy of conversion charge by RAJUK in the facts on the Property has led to an attempted conversion of the 1953 Act into a fiscal law even though the law books abound in separate fiscal statutes, such as the Income Tax Ordinance, 1984, for that very purpose. By that reason, the purported levy of conversion charge on the Property is found to be shorn of any authority or effect in law. Such finding is further reinforced by this Court's concern that the levy of such exorbitant amount of conversion fee or charge on the Petitioners has unavoidably rendered nugatory the Petitioners' intent to construct on the Property. That restriction is found to operate as an undue and illegal limitation on and constriction of the right to property guaranteed than under Article 42 of the Constitution.
